page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc7.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a baseline clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate solid compute and memory performance. The processor achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1579.99 and a multi-core score of 33336.85, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 31763.08. Memory bandwidth tests show read-only speeds of 1865.31 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 115.09 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, with write speeds reaching 52.5 GB/sec. In application-specific workloads, the instance achieves a static web serving throughput of 23.9 GB/sec and processes 31.19 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. For lightweight machine learning, the instance processes 1656.63 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 135M parameter LLM, dropping to 47.54 tokens per second on a 7B parameter model.

Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.hfc7.8xlarge is structured for compute-intensive tasks rather than memory-heavy databases or large-scale data caching. The lack of bundled local storage means all disk I/O must traverse the network, which may impact latency-sensitive storage operations. Qualitatively, the dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable performance, making it a cost-efficient choice for workloads requiring sustained CPU utilization without the overhead of unneeded RAM or GPU hardware. Recommended workloads include software compilation, web serving, multi-threaded decompression, and moderate-scale computational tasks.
